newsitem.title: GERMANY: Solana fears Moscow not clear on NATO intentions.
newsitem.headline: Solana fears Moscow not clear on NATO intentions.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said in an interview released on Wednesday he was worried Russia was misunderstanding the alliance's intentions on its future enlargement.
Solana, in an interview to appear in Thursday's General-Anzeiger daily in Bonn, said NATO had outlined to Moscow a plan for NATO enlargement which was reliable and could be trusted.
"Let me say what is personally important for me -- a stable, bilateral relationship between NATO and Moscow," Solana said, according to a text of his remarks released in advance.

"That is the most important thing for everyone involved. We know European security is not possible without or against Russia. But the Russian government is not realising the precise intentions of NATO."

NATO countries plan to name new members from central and eastern Europe at a July summit in Madrid, arguing that -- despite Moscow's virulent opposition -- the alliance's enlargement will help defuse potential regional flashpoints.
Critics of enlargement say it could end up having a destabilising effect, creating a new division in Europe.
Solana said the negotiations with Moscow were not designed to make "concessions" to Russia, but were instead aimed at finding mutual areas of cooperation.
He cited cooperation between NATO and Russian forces in former Yugoslavia as the type of operation he hoped to see carried out in the future.
